اكتشف خياراتك
الاستثمارية
الاستثمار بمدن الهيئة الملكية للجبيل وينبع

تعمل الهيئة الملكية للجبيل وينبع بشكل دائم ومستمر على تحسين تجربة المستثمرين بما يتوافق مع أهداف رؤية المملكة 2030، وذلك من خلال توحيد إجراءات الاستثمار وتحديث البوابات الإلكترونية. وقد عملت الهيئة على أتمتة بعض العمليات، مما ساهم في تقليل المدد الزمنية والمستندات المطلوبة للحصول على التصاريح والتراخيص، حيث استخدمت أحدث الأدوات والأساليب العلمية مثل (Six Sigma) وغيرها، مما أسهم في خلق بيئة استثمارية مرنة وجاذبة لمدنها الصناعية.

اكتشف المزيد
مجتمعنا
الحيوي
تنمية أنشئت بعناية ، فمنذ الخطوة الأولى على هذه الأرض عزمنا على تكوين مجتمعات حيوية متقدمة ومستدامة
تعليم رائد وطموح

التعليم.. تجربة متواصلة من الشغف والاستمتاع

رعاية طبية فائقة

تحرص الهيئة الملكية على توفير خدمات صحية فائقة في مدنها

نمط حياة مختلف

حياة صحية تتّسم بالجودة وتعزّز الرفاه في مدن الهيئة الملكية للجبيل وينبع

واقع سياحي جذاب

مدن الهيئة الملكية للجبيل وينبع ليست مجرد مراكز صناعية واقتصادية

مدننا
الصناعية
ولأن مدننا صممت لتكون الأفضل فنحن نعتني بزوارنا وسكاننا على أكمل وجه
مدينة الجبيل الصناعية
مدينة ينبع الصناعية
مدينة رأس الخير للصناعات التعدينية
مدينة جازان للصناعات الأساسية والتحويلية
مرتبطون
بالعالم

تتمتع الهيئة الملكية ببنية تحتية متطورة تدعم حركة البضائع والأشخاص، مثل المطارات التي تسهل النقل الجوي، والموانئ التي تمثل نقاطاً رئيسة للشحن البحري، والقطارات التي توفر وسيلة فعالة لنقل البضائع الثقيلة لمسافات طويلة. إضافة إلى ذلك، تؤدي شبكة الطرق والجسور دوراً حيوياً في تسهيل التنقل البري وربط المدن والمناطق، مما يعزز الكفاءة ويقلل التكاليف في عمليات النقل. وتعد هذه البنى التحتية أساسية لدعم التجارة والتنمية الاقتصادية.

إكتشف المزيد
حمايتنا
للبيئة

جهودنا في حماية البيئة والصناعة ترتكز على تحقيق التوازن بين النمو الاقتصادي والاستدامة البيئية. نحن نسعى لتقليل الأثر البيئي للصناعات من خلال تطبيق ممارسات صديقة للبيئة وتطوير تقنيات مستدامة

إكتشف المزيد
الهيئة الملكية نحو رؤية 2030 

الهيئة الملكية تواصل صناعة مستقبل المدن المتقدمة وتحقق قفزات تنموية في البنية التحتية والاقتصاد الصناعي

Boost Non-Profit Partnership","description":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"RIYADH — His Excellency Abdulmuhsen Al Mazyad, Vice Minister of Tourism, met today at the Ministry's headquarters with the chairmen of the Saudi Travel and Tourism Association, the Saudi Association for Tourism Accommodation Facilities, and the Saudi Tour Guides Association to discuss strengthening collaboration and partnership with the non-profit sector.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The meeting provided an opportunity to present the associations’ core roles, future directions, and strategic priorities. Discussions focused on key opportunities and challenges within the industry, as well as ways to deepen cooperation and integration with the Ministry. Participants also emphasized the vital role specialized associations play in advancing tourism activities, raising service standards, and expanding capacity-building programs for local talent.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The meeting reflects the Ministry of Tourism’s commitment to strengthening ties with the non-profit sector and expanding the role of of Tourism and Ministry of Investment Announce First Batch of Approved Projects under Hospitality Investment Enablers Program","shortDescription":"وزارة السياحة ووزارة الاستثمار تعتمدان المجموعة الأولى من المشاريع المستفيدة من برنامج ممكنات الاستثمار في قطاع الضيافة","description":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The Ministry of Tourism and the Ministry of Investment (MISA) have announced the first batch of projects approved under the Hospitality Investment Enablers (HIE) Program at a joint event held in Riyadh. The announcement ceremony was attended by His Excellency Ahmed Al Khateeb, Minister of Tourism, and His Excellency Fahad Al-Saif, Minister of Investment.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Under this program, the Ministry of Tourism – in cooperation with the Ministry of Investment – offers targeted enablers to accelerate private-sector investment in hospitality projects across selected tourism destinations in the Kingdom. The program helps reduce operating costs for approved hospitality projects, enhancing their economic viability and investment appeal.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"His Excellency Ahmed Al Khateeb said: “The Hospitality Investment Enablers Program reflects our long-standing commitment to enabling private-sector investment and responding to the Kingdom’s growing tourism demand. By expanding hospitality capacity in high-potential destinations, we are doing more than adding rooms. We are unlocking new investment opportunities, stimulating economic activity across tourism destinations, and supporting sustainable tourism growth. The first approved projects reflect investor confidence in the opportunities offered by Saudi Arabia’s tourism sector and the role of private-sector partnerships in turning these opportunities into projects that contribute to destination development.”","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"For his part, His Excellency Fahad Al-Saif affirmed that the tourism sector is a priority of the National Investment Strategy, given the significant investment opportunities it presents and its role in diversifying the economy and increasing its contribution to GDP, supporting the goals of Saudi Vision 2030.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"He added: “The Hospitality Investment Enablers Program is a model of government collaboration to develop enablers that strengthen private-sector participation, stimulate high-quality investment and develop the attractiveness of investment opportunities in promising tourism destinations. In partnership with the Ministry of Tourism and other relevant entities, we are working to strengthen the investment environment and simplify the investor journey, helping turn opportunities into sustainable projects, maximize their economic and developmental impact, create jobs and increase local content.”","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The first batch includes 19 projects across five high-potential tourism destinations. Together, they are expected to unlock SAR 6.7 billion in investment and create over 17,000 jobs. By 2030, the projects are expected to make an annual direct contribution of more than SAR 2.4 billion to GDP and contribute over SAR 5.3 billion to local content by generating demand for locally sourced goods, services, and materials.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The approved projects will add more than 3,000 hotel rooms to the Kingdom’s tourism supply. Approximately 40% of the planned rooms will be located in coastal destinations, strengthening the Kingdom’s sun-and-sea tourism offering.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The benefits will extend beyond accommodation, generating opportunities across food and beverage, retail, entertainment, and other visitor-focused services. This wider activity will support local businesses, stimulate economic growth in the participating destinations, and contribute to a more integrated visitor experience.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The first project is scheduled to open by the end of 2026, followed by further openings over the coming years, with the final projects set to become operational in 2029. This will expand the Kingdom’s hospitality capacity ahead of Expo 2030, the FIFA World Cup 2034, and other major international conferences and exhibitions.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"– Ends –.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"","type":"text"}]}],"slug":"ministry-of-tourism-and-ministry-of-investment-announce-first-batch-of-approved-projects-under-hospitality-investment-enablers-program","isFeatured":true,"date":"2026-10-19","createdAt":"2026-10-22T15:32:08.951Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-28T16:04:35.277Z","publishedAt":"2026-10-28T16:04:35.330Z","locale":"en","image":{"id":23251,"documentId":"vcjj3upm6t6t6jtbms7sb91p","name":"DSC_5032.webp","alternativeText":null,"caption":null,"width":5392,"height":2756,"formats":{"thumbnail":{"ext":".webp","url":"https://cdn.mt.gov.sa/mtweb/prod/uploads/thumbnail_DSC_5032_a631d8f136.webp","hash":"thumbnail_DSC_5032_a631d8f136","mime":"image/webp","name":"thumbnail_DSC_5032.webp","path":null,"size":8.59,"width":245,"height":125,"sizeInBytes":8592}},"hash":"DSC_5032_a631d8f136","ext":".webp","mime":"image/webp","size":934.28,"url":"https://cdn.mt.gov.sa/mtweb/prod/uploads/DSC_5032_a631d8f136.webp","previewUrl":null,"provider":"strapi-provider-upload-azure-storage","provider_metadata":null,"createdAt":"2026-10-22T15:31:22.431Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-22T15:31:22.431Z","publishedAt":"2026-10-22T15:31:22.432Z","focalPoint":null}},{"id":3410,"documentId":"ojbb9i9lqx4hespinix22kg7","title":"Saudi Tourism Minister Holds Talks with Bahrain’s Deputy Prime Minister","shortDescription":"وزير السياحة يلتقي نائب رئيس مجلس الوزراء البحريني","description":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":" His Excellency Ahmed Al Khateeb, Minister of Tourism, met today with His Excellency Shaikh Khalid bin Abdulla Al Khalifa, Deputy Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Bahrain, in the presence of Their Excellencies the GCC ministers responsible for tourism. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the 10th Meeting of the Ministers Responsible for Tourism in the GCC Countries in Manama.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"H.E. Al Khateeb expressed his appreciation to H.E. Shaikh Khalid bin Abdulla Al Khalifa for the warm welcome and generous hospitality. He affirmed the deep fraternal ties between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Kingdom of Bahrain, highlighting the close cooperation shared between the two countries across various sectors, particularly tourism.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The two sides discussed recent developments and growth prospects within the tourism sector, alongside strategies to strengthen regional cooperation among GCC member states. They also explored ongoing collaboration and knowledge exchange to bolster the sector's regional and international competitiveness, leveraging the continuous support of GCC leaders. //ENDS//","type":"text"}]}],"slug":"saudi-tourism-minister-holds-talks-with-bahrain-s-deputy-prime-minister","isFeatured":true,"date":"2026-10-09","createdAt":"2026-10-22T14:44:26.498Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-28T16:04:47.889Z","publishedAt":"2026-10-28T16:04:47.939Z","locale":"en","image":{"id":23250,"documentId":"ig1q1zzs2i0rfhnmfmw0k9uk","name":"Screenshot Stars\n","description":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"WEF and Saudi Arabia Announce First Cohort of Beyond Tourism Impact Stars","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"GENEVA/RIYADH, 25 September 2026 — Some of the world’s most impactful tourism solutions stepped onto a global stage today as the World Economic Forum (WEF), in partnership with the Ministry of Tourism of Saudi Arabia, unveiled the inaugural Beyond Tourism Impact Stars at the first Beyond Tourism Day in Geneva.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"On behalf of His Excellency Ahmed Al Khateeb, Saudi Arabia’s Minister of Tourism, Deputy Minister for Tourism Destinations Enablement Mahmoud Abdulhadi and Deputy Minister for International Affairs Hawazen Nassief represented the Ministry in its role as a global partner of WEF’s Beyond Tourism initiative and opened the inaugural Impact Stars announcement ceremony.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"In her remarks, Deputy Minister Nassief underlined the shared belief in the transformative power of tourism at the heart of the partnership between the Kingdom’s Ministry of Tourism and the World Economic Forum:","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"“Tourism can transform nations, diversify economies, improve livelihoods, sustain culture and heritage, and deepen understanding and human connection. The belief in the transformative power of tourism is at the heart of the Beyond Tourism partnership between the World Economic Forum and the Ministry of Tourism of Saudi Arabia. Together, we are committed to supporting practical models that drive progress in our sector.”","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The inaugural cohort spotlights six initiatives turning critical sector challenges into measurable, real-world solutions, including Sommet Education’s initiative to accelerate local hospitality workforce development through “Empowering Saudi Hospitality Talent.”","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Other winners include Accor via its global water conservation program; Discova (Singapore) for its support of community-led livelihoods across Asia; and GHE Impact Ventures (India) for combining clean energy with regenerative mountain tourism in “Himalayan Living Commons.” Completing the cohort are Al Ismaelia (Egypt) for historic urban restoration through “Reviving Downtown Cairo”; and Iberostar Group (Spain) for its data-driven hotel sustainability and marine stewardship in “Wave of Change.”","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Unlike conventional awards, Beyond Tourism Impact Stars is designed to take successful solutions further. The inaugural cohort will embark on a year-long journey of international engagement to amplify their proven models, facilitate knowledge exchange, and advance scalable adoption across emerging destinations.","type":"text"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Through the Ministry of Tourism’s partnership with WEF on the Beyond Tourism initiative, Saudi Arabia continues its role as a Development And Operation Of Strategic Water Storage Tanks – PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development of a strategic potable water storage system to ensure reliable and sustainable water supply and support AlUla’s economic and tourism growth and future development needs. The project includes the development and operation of five strategic water storage tanks with a combined capacity of 295,000 m³, providing approximately 3 to 4 days of potable water reserves, alongside pumping stations, connection networks, and supporting infrastructure serving urban districts, heritage sites, the airport, and new development areas. The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with a concession period of approximately 15 years, comprising 2 to 3 years of construction and 12 to 13 years of operations and maintenance, supported by availability-based payments linked to performance and water quality. The RFP is expected to be launched in Q4 2027, with phased completion targeted by 2031.

#RCU-OPP-000260
Learn More
Enhancement And Operation Of Wastewater Treatment Plants – PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the rehabilitation and expansion of the Wastewater Treatment Plant to increase treatment capacity, support economic growth, and enhance environmental sustainability. The project includes the rehabilitation of the existing plant with a capacity of 8,000 m³/day and its expansion using Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (MBBR) technology in two phases, adding 18,000 m³/day in Phase I and 36,000 m³/day in Phase II, bringing the total treatment capacity to 62,000 m³/day, alongside treated wastewater storage and pumping facilities, control systems, and supporting infrastructure. The project is planned to be delivered under a Build–Own–Operate–Transfer (BOOT) model, with a concession period of approximately 26 years, comprising 3 years of construction and rehabilitation and 23 years of operations, supported by capacity, output, and supplemental payments. The RFP is expected to be launched in Q2 2027.

#RCU-OPP-000259
Learn More
Development And Operation Of A Solid Waste Management System – PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development of an integrated solid waste management system in AlUla to enhance environmental sustainability, increase recycling rates, and support a sustainable economy. The project includes the development of a Resource Management Park and a waste transfer station with a capacity of 76,000 tonnes annually, recycling facilities with a capacity of 45,000 tonnes annually, organic waste treatment facilities, construction and demolition waste processing facilities with a capacity of 220,000 tonnes annually, and engineered landfill cells with a total capacity of 5 million cubic metres, alongside supporting infrastructure. The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with a concession period of 30 years, comprising 3 years of construction and 27 years of operations, supported by performance-based payments and waste gate and transfer fees. The RFP is planned to be launched in Q2 2027.

#RCU-OPP-000258
Learn More
Expansion Of Secondary Roads– PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development of the secondary road network to enhance connectivity, support economic and tourism growth in AlUla, and facilitate access to new development areas, heritage sites, and nature reserves. The project covers the development of 18 secondary road and utility corridors totalling approximately 1,400 km, including new road construction and integrated infrastructure for water supply, electricity, telecommunications, street lighting, and stormwater drainage. The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with an availability-based payment mechanism and a concession period of approximately 20 years. Operations and maintenance will cover roads only, with utilities handed over to the relevant entities. The RFP process for the project packages is planned to commence in early 2028, with phased completion targeted by 2033.

#RCU-OPP-000257
Learn More
Expansion Of Highways And Primary Roads – PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development and upgrade of the primary road network to enhance connectivity and support economic and tourism growth in AlUla. The project covers the development and upgrade of five primary roads and associated utility networks, totalling 204 km, including new road construction, rehabilitation, cycling paths, and traffic-calming measures, alongside integrated water, electricity, telecommunications, and stormwater drainage infrastructure. The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with an availability-based payment mechanism and a concession period of 15 years. Operations and maintenance will cover roads only, with utilities handed over to the relevant entities. The RFP process for the project packages is planned to commence in early 2028, with phased completion targeted by 2032.

#RCU-OPP-000256
Learn More
AlUla International Airport Expansion – PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Logistics & Industrial
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the expansion of AlUla International Airport to support economic and tourism growth and enhance AlUla’s air connectivity. The project includes a new passenger terminal of approximately 30,000 sqm, with a capacity of up to 3 million passengers annually, a 5,000 sqm cargo terminal incorporating world-class equestrian facilities, a private aviation terminal of approximately 10,000 sqm, general aviation and helicopter facilities, and an extension of the runway to 3,000 metres, in addition to roads, parking, maintenance facilities, utilities, and fuel facilities. Approximately 1 million sqm of land is also available for complementary commercial uses, including logistics, retail, hospitality, and aviation services. The project is planned to be delivered under a Build–Transfer–Operate (BTO) model, with a concession period of up to 35 years The RFP is expected to be launched in Q3 2027, with project completion targeted by 2032

","descriptionAR":"تماشيًا مع خطة التخصيص المعتمدة من المركز الوطني للتخصيص، تعمل الهيئة الملكية على تطوير منظومة استراتيجية لتخزين مياه الشرب، بهدف ضمان استدامة وموثوقية إمدادات المياه، ودعم النمو الاقتصادي والسياحي والاحتياجات المستقبلية للمحافظة.
